source: ཞེས་པ་སྟེ། སྒྲོལ་མ་ནི་དང་པོ་སྐུ་ཅི་ལས་བྱུང༌། བར་དུ་སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་དོན་ཅི་ལྟ་བུ་མཛད་ཅེ་ན། དང་པོ་འཇིག་རྟེན་གསུམ་གྱི་མགོན་པོ་འཕགས་པ་སྤྱན་རས་གཟིགས་དབང་ཕྱུག་གིས་གདུལ་བྱ་སེམས་ཅན་ཐམས་ཅད་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་གོ་འཕང་ལ་བཀོད་པར་མཛད་ན་ཡང་། སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་གནས་སྟོང་དུ་མེད་པ་མ་ཟད་སྡུག་བསྔལ་ཆེན་པོ་ཡོད་པ་ལ་བརྟེན་ནས། སྤྱན་ཆབ་མང་དུ་བསིལ་བས་ཆུ་ཡི་རྒྱུན་དུ་གྱུར། དེ་ལས་མེ་ཏོག་ཨུཏྤལ་ལ་སྐྱེས་ཏེ། དེ་ཡི་གེ་སར་ལས་འཁྲུངས་པས་ན། གེ་སར་བྱེ་བ་ལས་ནི་བྱུང་མ། །ཞེས་དང༌།
translation: This means: If one asks how the body of Tārā first arose and what kind of benefit she performs for sentient beings in the interim, it is as follows: Although the Noble Lord Avalokiteśvara, the protector of the three worlds, established all sentient beings to be tamed in the state of Buddhahood, he saw that the realms of sentient beings were not emptied and, furthermore, that they possessed great suffering. Relying on this, he shed many tears, which became a stream of water. From that, a lotus or utpala flower grew, and because she was born from its stamens, it is said, "Born from the opening stamens."

This means: If one asks how the body of Tārā first arose and what kind of benefit she performs for sentient beings in the interim, it is as follows: Although the Noble Lord Avalokiteśvara, the protector of the three worlds, established all sentient beings to be tamed in the state of Buddhahood, he saw that the realms of sentient beings were not emptied and, furthermore, that they possessed great suffering. Relying on this, he shed many tears, which became a stream of water. From that, a lotus or utpala flower grew, and because she was born from its stamens, it is said, "Born from the opening stamens."

If one wonders what kind of benefit she performs for those to be tamed after her birth, it is indicated by the words, "Homage to Tārā, the swift and heroic." She is "swift" because she acts quickly for the benefit of sentient beings, and she is a "heroine" because her courage is unyielding. That very Venerable Tārā, being thus swift and heroic, does not neglect to gaze with her wisdom eyes for the sake of sentient beings throughout the six times of the day and night. Because there is no obstruction to her vision in seeing who is in decline, who is flourishing, and so forth, it is said, "Whose eyes are like a flash of lightning." This means that I prostrate with devotion of the three doors to the Venerable One who possesses such qualities.

heading: དང་པོ་ཞལ་མདངས་གསལ་ཞིང་འོད་ཟེར་འཕྲོ་བའི་སྒོ་ནས་བསྟོད་པར་མཛད་པ།
translation: This means: In general, the moon is something that possesses a brilliance and luster that is superior to other objects. During the summer, it is obscured by clouds and mist, and during the winter, it is obscured by smoke and dust, making its brilliance unclear; however, during the autumn, it is free from both of these, and thus its brilliance is clear. Just as the moon on the fifteenth day possesses the quality of being full, the face of the Venerable One is also extremely clear and possesses brilliance, showing that it is of the same nature as the full autumn moon. Furthermore, regarding the instruction that light rays radiate from it, the phrase "by a thousand gathered stars" indicates that when a thousand stars are gathered together, they radiate light that is unbearable for the eyes to behold; in the same way, light and rays of light radiate from the face of the Venerable One that are unbearable for the eyes to behold. Thus, this is a prostration by way of the qualities of having a beautiful face and radiating light.

The second section concerns prostrating by way of the aspects of the body, which is divided into two: prostrating by way of the aspect of the Sambhogakāya and prostrating by way of the aspect of the Dharmakāya. The first of these, prostrating by way of the aspect of the Sambhogakāya, is further divided into two: prostrating by way of the peaceful aspect and prostrating by way of the wrathful aspect. The first of these, which praises her by way of her clear, radiant complexion and the light rays she emits, is:

With a gold and blue water-born lotus,

Generosity, diligence, austerity, peace,
Patience, and meditative concentration.

ཞེས་པ་སྟེ། སྤྱིར་ཟླ་བ་དེ་དངོས་པོ་གཞན་ལས་ཁྱད་པར་དུ་འཕགས་པ་བཀྲག་མདངས་དང་ལྡན་པ་ཞིག་ཡིན་ལ། དབྱར་གྱི་དུས་སུ་སྤྲིན་དང་རླངས་པས་སྒྲིབ་ཅིང་། དགུན་གྱི་དུས་སུ་དུ་བ་དང་ས་རྡུལ་གྱིས་སྒྲིབ་ནས་བཀྲག་མདངས་མི་གསལ་བ་ཡིན་ནའང་། སྟོན་གྱི་དུས་སུ་དེ་གཉིས་ཀ་དང་བྲལ་བས་བཀྲག་མདངས་གསལ་བ་ཡིན་ལ། ཚེས་བཅོ་ལྔའི་ཟླ་བ་ནི་གང་བའི་ཆ་དང་ལྡན་པ་དེ་བཞིན་དུ། རྗེ་བཙུན་གྱི་ཞལ་རས་ཀྱང་ཤིན་ཏུ་གསལ་ཞིང་བཀྲག་མདངས་དང་ལྡན་པ། སྟོན་ཀའི་ཟླ་བ་ཉ་གང་བ་དང་ཆོས་མཚུངས་པར་བསྟན་པ་དང༌། དེ་ལས་འོད་ཟེར་འཕྲོ་བར་བསྟན་པར་མཛད་པ་ནི། སྐར་མ་སྟོང་ཕྲག་ཚོགས་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱིས། །ཞེས་སྐར་མ་སྟོང་ཕྲག་ཙམ་གཅིག་ཏུ་འཚོགས་པ་ན་འོད་ཟེར་ཀྱང་མིག་གི་ལྟ་བས་མི་བཟོད་པར་འཕྲོ་བ་དེ་བཞིན་དུ་རྗེ་བཙུན་མའི་ཞལ་རས་ལས་ཀྱང་འོད་དང་འོད་ཟེར་མིག་གིས་ལྟ་བས་མི་བཟོད་པར་འཕྲོ་བ་སྟེ། ཞལ་རས་མཛེས་པ་དང་། འོད་ཟེར་འཕྲོ་བའི་ཡོན་ཏན་དང་ལྡན་པའི་སྒོ་ནས་ཕྱག་འཚལ་བ་དང༌།

This means: In general, the moon is something that possesses a brilliance and luster that is superior to other objects. During the summer, it is obscured by clouds and mist, and during the winter, it is obscured by smoke and dust, making its brilliance unclear; however, during the autumn, it is free from both of these, and thus its brilliance is clear. Just as the moon on the fifteenth day possesses the quality of being full, the face of the Venerable One is also extremely clear and possesses brilliance, showing that it is of the same nature as the full autumn moon. Furthermore, regarding the instruction that light rays radiate from it, the phrase "by a thousand gathered stars" indicates that when a thousand stars are gathered together, they radiate light that is unbearable for the eyes to behold; in the same way, light and rays of light radiate from the face of the Venerable One that are unbearable for the eyes to behold. Thus, this is a prostration by way of the qualities of having a beautiful face and radiating light.

heading: གཉིས་པ་སྐུ་མདོག་དང་ཕྱག་མཚན་དང་སྐུའི་སྒོ་ནས་བསྟོད་པར་མཛད་པ།
source: ཞེས་པ་སྟེ། སྐུ་མདོག་གི་དབང་དུ་ན། གསེར་སྔོ་ཆུ་ནས་སྐྱེས་ཀྱི། ཞེས་མདངས་ཤིན་ཏུ་གསལ་བའི་ཆ་ནས་གསེར་གྱི་མདངས་དང་ཆོས་མཚུངས་ཤིང་། ཁ་དོག་གི་བཀྲག་མདངས་དངོས་སུ་མེད་པར་སྔོན་པོའི་རྣམ་པ་དང་ལྡན་པར་བསྟན་པར་མཛད་པ་དང་། ཕྱག་མཚན་གྱི་དབང་དུ་ན། ཆུ་ནས་སྐྱེས་ཀྱི་སྟེ། པདྨས་ཕྱག་ནི་རྣམ་པར་བརྒྱན་མ། །ཞེས་དེ་ལ་ཆུ་ལས་སྐྱེས་པའི་མེ་ཏོག་ཨུཏྤལ་སྔོན་པོ་འདབ་མ་ཤིན་ཏུ་ཡངས་ཤིང་རྒྱ་ཆེ་བ་ཕྱག་གཡོན་པས་ཐུགས་ཀར་འཛིན་ཅིང་འདབ་མ་སྙན་གྱི་ཐད་ཀར་ཕྱེ་བ་དེ་སྐུའི་ཡོན་ཏན་དང་ལྡན་པ་བསྟན་པར་མཛད་པ་དང༌།
translation: This means: Regarding the body color, the phrase "gold and blue water-born" indicates that, in terms of being extremely bright, it is of the same nature as the luster of gold, while showing that it possesses a blue appearance without having the actual luster of a colored pigment. Regarding the hand symbols, the phrase "water-born" refers to the lotus, and "her hand is perfectly adorned with a lotus" indicates that she holds a blue utpala flower—which is born from water and has very wide and expansive petals—at her heart with her left hand, with the petals blossoming at the level of her ear, thereby showing that she possesses the qualities of the body.

heading: གཉིས་པ་སྐུ་མདོག་དང་ཕྱག་མཚན་དང་སྐུའི་སྒོ་ནས་བསྟོད་པར་མཛད་པ།
source: སྐུའི་དབང་དུ་ན། རྗེ་བཙུན་མ་ནི་སྐུ་གང་ལས་བྱུང་སྙམ་ན། རྒྱུ་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་དྲུག་ལས་བྱུང་བ་ཡིན་ཏེ་དང་པོ་སྦྱིན་པའི་ཕར་ཕྱིན་དང༌། དཀའ་ཐུབ་ནི་ཚུལ་ཁྲིམས་ཀྱི་ཕར་ཕྱིན། བཟོད་པའི་ཕར་ཕྱིན། བརྩོན་འགྲུས་ཀྱི་ཕར་ཕྱིན། བསམ་གཏན་གྱི་ཕར་ཕྱིན། བསམ་གཏན་གྱི་སྤྱོད་ཡུལ་ཞེས་པ་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་སྟེ། ཕར་ཕྱིན་དྲུག་ལ་བརྟེན་ནས་བསྐྱེད་པ་ཡིན་ཞིང་། རྒྱུ་ཕར་ཕྱིན་དྲུག་གིས་བསྐྱེད་པ་ཙམ་དུ་མ་ཟད། ཞི་བ་ཞེས་པས་དངོས་བསྟན་གྱི་དབང་དུ་བྱས་ན། ཕྱིན་དྲུག་ལ་སྐྱོན་གྱི་རྣམ་པས་མ་གོས་པ་སྟེ།
translation: Regarding the body, if one wonders from what the Noble Lady’s body arises, it arises from the six perfections: first is the perfection of generosity, and "austerity" is the perfection of ethical discipline, the perfection of patience, the perfection of diligence, the perfection of meditative concentration, and the phrase "sphere of activity of meditative concentration" is the perfection of wisdom. Thus, it is generated by relying on the six perfections. Not only is it generated by the six perfections as causes, but if we take the term "peace" in terms of its direct indication, it means that the six perfections are not tainted by any form of defect.

translation: She suppresses them with her two feet: the foot that perceives emptiness and the foot that does not abandon others out of compassion. By doing so, she protects them from the suffering of cyclic existence and the lower realms, and she possesses the quality of being able to summon all sentient beings of cyclic existence—leaving none behind in the lower realms—onto the path of higher status and liberation; thus, it is shown that one pays homage by way of her suppressing all discordant factors.

translation: This means: Her left hand, with the thumb and ring finger joined at her heart and the index, middle, and little fingers raised, is the mudrā symbolizing the Three Jewels; with the thumb and ring finger, she beautifully adorns her heart with the stem of an utpala flower. With her right hand, she performs the mudrā of supreme generosity, which symbolizes the granting of supreme and common accomplishments to all sentient beings without exception; the palm is beautifully adorned with the design of a thousand-spoked wheel, and because the light rays from it dispel all the masses of harm to all sentient beings and bestow all aspects of benefit and happiness, this is a praise by way of her causing a boundless, swirling mass of light from the wheel itself.

heading: གསུམ་པ་དབུ་རྒྱན་དང་བཞད་པའི་སྒོ་ནས་བསྟོད་པར་མཛད་པ།
translation: This means: The noble lady herself possesses supreme joy in bestowing all benefit and happiness upon sentient beings without exception, and she possesses great courage in being diligent in that task. By the power of spreading boundless garlands of light and rays from the tip of her crown ornament, which symbolizes the five families, she bestows all benefit and happiness upon sentient beings. The praise by way of laughter means that, through laughter, great laughter, and so forth, she strikes terror into all hosts of maras and enemies, and brings all three worlds under her power or subjugation.

source: ཞེས་པ་སྟེ། ས་གཞི་སྐྱོང་བ་ནི་ཕྱོགས་སྐྱོང་བཅུ་པོ་སྟེ་སྟེང་དུ་ཚངས་པ། ཤར་དུ་བརྒྱ་བྱིན། ཤར་ལྷོར་མེ་ལྷ། ལྷོར་གཤིན་རྗེ། ལྷོ་ནུབ་ཏུ་སྲིན་པོ།ནུབ་བྱང་དུ་རླུང་ལྷ། བྱང་དུ་གནོད་སྦྱིན། བྱང་ཤར་དུ་དབང་ལྡན། འོག་ཏུ་ས་བདག་བཅས་ཀྱི་ཚོགས་རྣམས་དང༌། དེའི་འཁོར་དང་བཅས་པ་ཐམས་ཅད་རྗེ་བཙུན་མའི་ཐུགས་ཀའི་ཏཱཾ་གྱི་འོད་ཟེར་གྱིས་བཀུག་པར་མཛད་ཅིང༌། ཅི་བཅོལ་བའི་ལས་ཐམས་ཅད་སྒྲུབ་པ་དང༌།
translation: This means: "Those who protect the earth" are the ten directional protectors, namely: Brahmā above, Indra in the east, Agni in the southeast, Yama in the south, Rākṣasa in the southwest, Varuṇa in the west, Vāyu in the northwest, Yakṣa in the north, Īśāna in the northeast, and the Earth Lord below. The noble lady summons all these hosts, along with their retinues, by means of the light rays from the TĀṀ at her heart, and she accomplishes all tasks that are entrusted to her.

translation: Regarding the hosts of powerful spirits who do not abide by the vows of the commands given in this way, the noble lady causes the wrinkles on her fiercely wrathful face to quiver like clouds, and from the HŪṀ at her heart, she emanates immeasurable hosts of HŪṀs and wrathful ones, thereby praising her by way of establishing all those beings to be tamed—who are destitute of emptiness and compassion, who possess negative karma, and who engage in suffering and non-virtue—in the state of the omniscient Buddha.

Homage to you, who are able to summon
All the hosts of those who protect the earth;
With the syllable HŪṀ and a quivering frown,
You completely liberate from all destitution.

[2-47] source:

This means: "Those who protect the earth" are the ten directional protectors, namely: Brahmā above, Indra in the east, Agni in the southeast, Yama in the south, Rākṣasa in the southwest, Varuṇa in the west, Vāyu in the northwest, Yakṣa in the north, Īśāna in the northeast, and the Earth Lord below. The noble lady summons all these hosts, along with their retinues, by means of the light rays from the TĀṀ at her heart, and she accomplishes all tasks that are entrusted to her.

Regarding the hosts of powerful spirits who do not abide by the vows of the commands given in this way, the noble lady causes the wrinkles on her fiercely wrathful face to quiver like clouds, and from the HŪṀ at her heart, she emanates immeasurable hosts of HŪṀs and wrathful ones, thereby praising her by way of establishing all those beings to be tamed—who are destitute of emptiness and compassion, who possess negative karma, and who engage in suffering and non-virtue—in the state of the omniscient Buddha.

heading: དྲུག་པ་རྗེ་བཙུན་མ་དེ་ཉིད་ཁྲོ་མོར་བཞུགས་ཚུལ་གྱི་སྒོ་ནས་བསྟོད་པར་མཛད་པ།
translation:
Homage to you, who dwell in the midst of a garland of fire
That blazes like the fire at the end of an eon;
With right leg extended and left bent, you are surrounded by joy,
And you completely destroy the armies of enemies.

translation: This means: She presses down upon the surface of this great earth, the foundation of the world, with the palms of both hands and strikes it forcefully with the soles of both feet. She possesses a wrathful face with a frown, and her two eyes are intensely agitated, their light rays pervading all directions. From the dark blue HŪṂ syllable at her heart, immeasurable light rays radiate, protecting or bringing goodness to all sentient beings residing in the seven levels—the three lower realms, the three higher realms, and the desire and form realms combined—by saving them from all temporary and ultimate suffering. Thus, she is praised by way of the seven homages to the wrathful form.

heading: གཉིས་པ་ཆོས་སྐུའི་རྣམ་པའི་སྒོ་ནས་བསྟོད་པར་མཛད་པ།
translation: This means: Because she has already abandoned all that is to be abandoned by the path of seeing, she is free from suffering and possesses perfect bliss; thus, she is the "Blissful One." Because she uproots all that is to be abandoned by the path of meditation, she manifests the fruit through the path of perfect virtue; thus, she is the "Virtuous One." Because all stains of habitual tendencies have become completely pacified, she is the "Peaceful One." Being free from all stains of the three obscurations, she is the Noble Lady herself, who possesses the sphere of experience of the peace of nirvāṇa. The manifestation of the wisdom of the path of seeing, the wisdom of the path of meditation, and ultimately the wisdom of all that is and all that exists, constitutes the qualities of her heart, the Dharmakāya.

heading: གཉིས་པ་ཆོས་སྐུའི་རྣམ་པའི་སྒོ་ནས་བསྟོད་པར་མཛད་པ།
translation: The ten syllables of the Noble Lady’s mantra, adorned at the end with SVĀHĀ and at the beginning with OṂ, protect those to be tamed from the eight and sixteen fears in the short term, and ultimately from all the sufferings of cyclic existence and the lower realms; this constitutes the qualities of her speech, the Sambhogakāya. Following that, because one confesses in the proper manner before the Noble Lady—who possesses a body that is a collection of the major and minor marks—all the great negativity, the ten non-virtuous actions, and the five inexpiable crimes that I and all sentient beings have committed, she utterly destroys all negativity and obscurations from the root; this constitutes the qualities of her body. Thus, the praise is offered by way of the qualities of body, speech, and mind.

[2-60] translation already produced for this document:
This means: Because she has already abandoned all that is to be abandoned by the path of seeing, she is free from suffering and possesses perfect bliss; thus, she is the "Blissful One." Because she uproots all that is to be abandoned by the path of meditation, she manifests the fruit through the path of perfect virtue; thus, she is the "Virtuous One." Because all stains of habitual tendencies have become completely pacified, she is the "Peaceful One." Being free from all stains of the three obscurations, she is the Noble Lady herself, who possesses the sphere of experience of the peace of nirvāṇa. The manifestation of the wisdom of the path of seeing, the wisdom of the path of meditation, and ultimately the wisdom of all that is and all that exists, constitutes the qualities of her heart, the Dharmakāya.

heading: དང་པོ་རྩ་བའི་སྔགས་ཀྱི་ཕྲིན་ལས་བསྟན་པའི་སྒོ་ནས་བསྟོད་པར་མཛད་པ།
translation:
Homage to you, surrounded by joy,
Who utterly shatters the bodies of enemies;
With the ten-syllable speech arranged,
You are Tārā, emerging from the HŪṂ of awareness.

heading: དང་པོ་རྩ་བའི་སྔགས་ཀྱི་ཕྲིན་ལས་བསྟན་པའི་སྒོ་ནས་བསྟོད་པར་མཛད་པ།
translation: This means that, of the two—peaceful and wrathful—the peaceful mantra is the ten-syllable one, while the mantra for performing the wrathful method is OṂ TĀRE HŪṂ HARA HARA HŪṂ, which contains two "HARA" syllables and is the mantra of the wrathful type. Thus, by way of the peaceful and wrathful mantras, and through the power of being surrounded by joy and having a mind of pure faith toward the Noble Lady, the hosts of enemy forces that harm and injure those individuals are thoroughly and utterly shattered by means of the peaceful and wrathful mantra forms; this constitutes the praise offered by way of indicating the benefits of the mantra.

The ten syllables of the Noble Lady’s mantra, adorned at the end with SVĀHĀ and at the beginning with OṂ, protect those to be tamed from the eight and sixteen fears in the short term, and ultimately from all the sufferings of cyclic existence and the lower realms; this constitutes the qualities of her speech, the Sambhogakāya. Following that, because one confesses in the proper manner before the Noble Lady—who possesses a body that is a collection of the major and minor marks—all the great negativity, the ten non-virtuous actions, and the five inexpiable crimes that I and all sentient beings have committed, she utterly destroys all negativity and obscurations from the root; this constitutes the qualities of her body. Thus, the praise is offered by way of the qualities of body, speech, and mind.

heading: གཉིས་པ་ཁྲོ་མོའི་བཞུགས་ཚུལ་གྱིས་ཁམས་གསུམ་གནོན་པའི་སྒོ་ནས་བསྟོད་པར་མཛད་པ།

This means that, of the two—peaceful and wrathful—the peaceful mantra is the ten-syllable one, while the mantra for performing the wrathful method is OṂ TĀRE HŪṂ HARA HARA HŪṂ, which contains two "HARA" syllables and is the mantra of the wrathful type. Thus, by way of the peaceful and wrathful mantras, and through the power of being surrounded by joy and having a mind of pure faith toward the Noble Lady, the hosts of enemy forces that harm and injure those individuals are thoroughly and utterly shattered by means of the peaceful and wrathful mantra forms; this constitutes the praise offered by way of indicating the benefits of the mantra.

Homage to you, who holds in your hand the deer-marked one,
Which has the form of a celestial lake;
By reciting TĀRA twice and the syllable PHAṬ,
You are the one who eliminates all poisons without exception.

heading: གསུམ་པ་བརྟན་གཡོའི་དུག་ཐམས་ཅད་སེལ་བར་མཛད་པའི་སྒོ་ནས་བསྟོད་པར་མཛད་པ།
translation: This means that the full moon mandala is in the form of a nectar lake that is delightful to the gods. Upon the open utpala flower in her left hand, she holds the deer-marked one, or the full moon. From the sound of the mantra of reciting TĀRA twice from her mouth, light rays like droplets of nectar emerge, and from the full moon as well, a stream of nectar descends. By this stream of nectar pervading all the poisons of the moving—the ignorance and the collection of mental afflictions of all sentient beings—and all the collections of types of poisons, such as the compounded poisons of the stable, this constitutes the praise by way of eliminating all collections of harm from mental afflictions and poisons.

Even though she is relied upon by gods and kinnaras, she acts as an armor or protection that guards those who rely upon her at all times so that no evil omens occur. heading: དྲུག་པ་གདོན་དང་རོ་ལངས་འཇོམས་པའི་ཕྲིན་ལས་བསྟན་པ།
translation:
Homage to her, established by the three suchnesses,
Perfectly endowed with the power of pacification;
She is the supreme Ture who destroys
The hosts of spirits, zombies, and yakṣas.

heading: དྲུག་པ་གདོན་དང་རོ་ལངས་འཇོམས་པའི་ཕྲིན་ལས་བསྟན་པ།
translation: This means that the suchness of the body is the white syllable Oṃ, the suchness of the speech is the red syllable Āḥ, and the suchness of the mind is the blue syllable Hūṃ. By arranging these three suchnesses at the three places of her body and praying single-pointedly to be protected from all fears and sufferings, one is protected by the venerable Tārā, who possesses the perfect power to pacify all temporary and ultimate sufferings. From her three places, she emits three light rays, which subdue all the harms caused by the hosts of spirits, zombies, and yakṣas to those to be tamed, and this constitutes the praise by way of granting the supreme or excellent wishes of Ture.

heading: དང་པོ་བསམ་པ་བསྟན་པ།

By any intelligent person
Endowed with genuine devotion to the Goddess,
Who recites this clearly,

heading: གཉིས་པ་དུས་ཀྱི་དབང་དུ་ན།

heading: གསུམ་པ་ཕན་ཡོན་དངོས་བསྟན་པ།
translation:
Seventy million Victorious Ones
Will swiftly confer empowerment,
And one will attain even greater significance than this,
And proceed to that ultimate state of Buddhahood.

heading: གསུམ་པ་ཕན་ཡོན་དངོས་བསྟན་པ།
translation: This means that, by relying on the power of making single-pointed supplication to that very Bhagavatī—who was empowered by seventy million Victorious Ones throughout the worlds of the ten directions as the Mother, the Perfection of Wisdom—one will, in this very life, attain the temporary qualities of the higher realms. Their poisons, which are extremely fierce,
Whether stationary or moving,
Even if eaten or drunk,
Are completely eliminated by remembering [her].

heading: གསུམ་པ་ཕན་ཡོན་དངོས་བསྟན་པ།
translation: This means that, regarding the time for any person, the obscurations of poison that obstruct the path to attaining the state of Buddhahood—the three obscurations that destroy all the happiness of the state of liberation, which are like the fierce and great [poisons]—are all abandoned by relying on making single-pointed supplication to the Bhagavatī. Furthermore, regarding "stationary or moving," all the obscurations accumulated in the minds of all sentient beings since beginningless time remain fixed until they are destroyed by the vajra-like concentration of the end of the continuum.

[3-13] translation already produced for this document:
"Moving," refers to all other types of poisons that move and circulate, such as those of snakes, as well as the poisons of fangs, the poisons of flesh, the poisons of fur, and so forth; all such types of poison are pacified. "Even if eaten or drunk," means that in the same way, for all sentient beings who have eaten or drunk such things and are experiencing unbearable suffering, if those individuals make single-pointed supplication to the Bhagavatī,

[3-14] source:
དྲན་པས་རབ་ཏུ་སེལ་བ་ཉིད་འཐོབ། །ཅེས་རྗེ་བཙུན་མའི་བྱིན་རླབས་དྲན་པ་ཙམ་གྱིས་རབ་ཏུ་བདེ་བ་ཁྱད་པར་ཅན་ཐོབ་སྟེ། སྡུག་བསྔལ་དེ་དག་སེལ་བ་ཉིད་ནི་འཐོབ་པ་དང༌།
[3-14] translation already produced for this document:
"Are completely eliminated by remembering [her]," means that by merely remembering the blessings of the Bhagavatī, one attains a supreme and special happiness, and thus one attains the complete elimination of those sufferings.

[3-15] source:
གདོན་དང་རིམས་དང་དུག་གིས་གཟིར་བའི། །
སྡུག་བསྔལ་ཚོགས་ནི་རྣམ་པར་སྤོང་སྟེ། །
སེམས་ཅན་གཞན་པ་རྣམས་ལ་ཡང་ངོ་། །

heading: བཞི་པ་གྲངས་ཀྱི་སྒོ་ནས་མཇུག་བསྡུ་བ།
translation:
If recited two, three, or seven times,
Those desiring a child will obtain a child,
Those desiring wealth will obtain wealth,
All desires will be attained,
And obstacles will be non-existent and individually destroyed.

heading: བཞི་པ་གྲངས་ཀྱི་སྒོ་ནས་མཇུག་བསྡུ་བ།
translation: This means that if one recites this to the Bhagavatī with a mind of supreme faith two, three, or seven times, the reciter will attain all that they desire in the interim, such as children and wealth. The ultimate desire, the permanent happiness of the state of Buddhahood, will also be attained, and until that is attained, may all obstacles and hindrances be individually destroyed by relying upon the blessings of the Bhagavatī.

[3-16] translation already produced for this document:
Furthermore, "Tormented by demons, infectious diseases, and poisons, the masses of suffering are thoroughly abandoned," means that the masses of suffering—constantly tormenting and afflicting one through demons that constitute a host of harms, infectious diseases caused by the disturbance of the elements, and various types of poisons—are completely and thoroughly abandoned the moment one makes supplication to the Bhagavatī. "And this applies to other sentient beings as well," means that by merely making supplication to the Bhagavatī through the twenty-one prostrations, one not only accomplishes one's own benefit, but also acts to protect all other sentient beings from whatever suffering they may have.

This means: In general, the moon is something that possesses a brilliance and luster that is superior to other objects. During the summer, it is obscured by clouds and mist, and during the winter, it is obscured by smoke and dust, making its brilliance unclear; however, during the autumn, it is free from both of these, and thus its brilliance is clear. Just as the moon on the fifteenth day possesses the quality of being full, the face of the Venerable One is also extremely clear and possesses brilliance, showing that it is of the same nature as the full autumn moon. Furthermore, regarding the instruction that light rays radiate from it, the phrase "by a thousand gathered stars" indicates that when a thousand stars are gathered together, they radiate light that is unbearable for the eyes to behold; in the same way, light and rays of light radiate from the face of the Venerable One that are unbearable for the eyes to behold. Thus, this is a prostration by way of the qualities of having a beautiful face and radiating light.
